en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Tenth Chapter
Discourse on Matter as the Path:
Is the matter of one who possesses the path the path? Yes.
“Does it have an object? Is there for it turning toward, mental engagement, attention, volition, aspiration, and resolve?
“One should not say so.
“… Is it not rather without an object, and is there for it no turning toward … nor aspiration?”
“Yes.
“If it has no object, then there is for it no turning toward [the object], nor … [nor] aspiration.
Indeed, you should not say:”
“Is the matter of one possessing the path the path?
Yes. “Is right speech the path? Yes.
"Does it have an object? Is there, for that [consciousness], turning toward...
aspiration? "One should not say so. ...
"Is it then without an object? Is there, for that, no turning toward... aspiration?"
“Yes.
“If it has no object, then there is no turning toward it … [and so on] … nor aspiration.
Indeed, you should not say that.”
“Right speech is the path.
Is right action ...
[and] right livelihood the path?
“Yes,” [you reply].
“Does it have an object; does it have a turning toward it ... pe ... a longing for it?
You should not say so ... pe ...
But is it not the case that it is without an object, and for it there is no turning toward [the object], nor... nor aspiration?
Yes, it is so.
If it is indeed without an object, and for it there is no turning toward [the object], nor... nor aspiration; [then how can it be called "directed"]?
And indeed, it should not be said that "right livelihood is the path.
Right view is the path, and it has an object; there is turning by means of it … [and so on] … up to … aspiration?
“Yes,” you say.
“Right speech is the path, and it has an object; does it have turning toward [the object] … pe … aspiration?
You must not say so … pe …
Right view is the path, and it has an object; is there, by means of it, turning toward [the object] …pe… aspiration?
Yes. Right action …pe… [is the same].
Right livelihood is the path, and it has an object; there is its turning toward [the goal] …pe… its aspiration—is this not so?
One should not say so …pe… [and the same applies to] right intention …pe…
Right effort ... [and so on] ...
right mindfulness ... [and so on] ...
Right concentration is the path; and it has an object, and there is its turning toward, ... [and so on] ... its aspiration, is that not so?
“Yes,” you say.
“Right speech is the path, and it has an object; does it have turning toward [the object] … pe … aspiration?
You must not say so … pe …
Right concentration is the path, and it has an object; is there for it turning toward [the object] … pe … aspiration?
Yes. Right action … pe … [and so on].
Right livelihood is the path, and it has an object; does it have turning toward [the object], and so forth, up to aspiration?
You should not say so...
Right speech is the path, and it has no object; does it lack turning toward [an object], and so forth, up to aspiration?
“Yes,” you say.
“Right view is the path, yet it has no object; there is no turning toward it … [and so on] … nor aspiration for it?
You must not speak thus … [and so on].
Right speech is the path, yet it is without an object; there is no turning toward it … [and so on] … nor aspiration?
Yes. Right intention … [and so on] …
Right effort … right mindfulness … right concentration is the path, yet it has no object; there is no turning toward it … nor any aspiration for it?
One should not say this … [and so on] … Right action … [and so on].
Right livelihood is the path, and it is without an object; there is no turning toward it … nor aspiration for it?
Yes. [Is this true] of right view … right intention … right effort … right mindfulness … and so forth? Yes.
“Right concentration is the path, yet it is without an object; there is for it no turning toward, nor even aspiration”?
One should not speak thus … [as before] … One should not speak thus.
“Is the form of one possessing the path the path?”—
Yes. But is it not the case that right speech, right action, and right livelihood are the path?
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “If right speech, right action, and right livelihood are the Path, then indeed it must be said:
‘The form of one who possesses the Path is the Path.’”
The discussion on form as the path is finished.
